title: [CQ-M07f] Guest supervisor reset mode for seat VM reuse
description:
Slice of CQ-M07 (task-1a8f1d0e199046a289e94a5453d758b8). Design: mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation, decision 1 (human, 2026-11-01: one VM per seat, plus a reset mode).

GATE: BACKLOG until task-fd196d13's transport design has its governor ruling; then move it to PLANNING. It depends on fd196d13 because both change scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py and the host stream code. HIGH: the human chose to sequence it right after fd196d13 so ONE operator re-certify on Windows and Linux covers both pin moves.

Objective: the host can return a seat's VM to a clean workspace between jobs. materialize refuses an existing workspace or manifest with EX_CANTCREAT (guest-supervisor.py materialize), so reusing a VM needs a root-only reset.

Deliverable:
- guest-supervisor.py: a root-only `reset` mode. It refuses with a new fixed sysexits-style code (document it in the header with the codes already taken) while any moe-agent or moe-check process exists. Otherwise it removes WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MANIFEST and the old per-job session homes WITHOUT following symlinks (fd-based removal; refuse if the interpreter's rmtree cannot avoid symlink attacks), and leaves the toolchain, the agent binaries, the bootstrap files and the readiness state intact. Optional, only if trivial: delete moe-agent-owned entries in /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm (the human accepted that residue; do not let it grow the slice).
- Host side: resetWorkspace next to materializeSnapshot in scripts/local-runner/snapshot-transfer.mjs, over whatever transport fd196d13 lands, mapping each supervisor exit to a fixed code. No fallback.
- This moves R13's certified supervisor sha (3a19f3bf...). The completion names the new sha256 and posts it on R13 (task-f4811a72) and on CQ-M07.

NOT in scope: deciding when reset runs (CQ-M07j); any loosening of materialize, export, readiness, the job guarantees or certified-provider.json.

Verification: in a git-archive snapshot of `scripts packages/moe-daemon/src packages/moe-daemon/package.json packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json .github` with this task's files overlaid: env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs plus the supervisor rows' file if they live elsewhere (mem:gotcha-local-runner-supervisor-tests).
definitionOfDone: reset removes the workspace, its manifest and the session homes and exits 0, and a following materialize then succeeds (real-python rows with injected paths).
reset refuses with its fixed code and removes nothing while a moe-agent or moe-check process is alive (row with an injected process probe).
A symlink planted in the workspace and pointing outside it is removed as a link while its target is untouched (real-python row).
Toolchain, agent binaries and bootstrap files survive reset (row).
Host resetWorkspace maps every supervisor exit to a fixed code with fakes, with no fallback (rows).
The local-runner suite passes in a git-archive snapshot; the completion summary names the new guest-supervisor.py sha256.
taskRails: Do not loosen guest readiness, the certified-provider.json pins or any existing guest-supervisor.py guarantee.
No seat runs Multipass; the real-guest proof is the operator's re-certify.

implementationPlan.description:
Add a root-only `reset` mode to scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py (mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation decision 1; mem:gotcha-local-runner-supervisor-tests).
(1) `RESET_BUSY = os.EX_UNAVAILABLE` (69). 69 is free: taken today are 0, 64-66, 71, 73-77, 79-82, and 78 is retired.
(2) `def identity_alive(uids, proc='/proc')`. Scan the numeric entries of /proc and read each `<pid>/status` Uid: line (real, effective, saved, fs). Return True if any uid is in `uids`.
  - A pid that vanishes mid-read (FileNotFoundError or ProcessLookupError) is skipped.
  - Any other OSError propagates, so reset fails closed.
  - The root PID namespace's /proc lists jobs inside their own PID namespaces too.
(3) `def reset(out_fd, workspace=WORKSPACE, manifest=WORKSPACE_MANIFEST, sessions=SESSIONS, uids=None, alive=identity_alive)`, in this order:
  - uids None: resolve AGENT_IDENTITY and CHECK_IDENTITY with pwd, KeyError → 71;
  - `if not shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks: return os.EX_OSERR` (71). The fd-based rmtree is required.
  - `if alive(set(uids)): return RESET_BUSY`, removing nothing;
  - remove workspace: lstat, ENOENT is fine; a directory goes through shutil.rmtree, anything else (link, file) through os.unlink, so a link at the root is never followed;
  - remove manifest: os.unlink, ENOENT is fine;
  - for each name in os.listdir(sessions) starting with 'home-' (a missing sessions dir is fine), the same lstat rule: rmtree a directory, else unlink. sessions itself stays.
  - write_frame(out_fd, {'kind': 'reset'}) and return 0.
  Error handling: any OSError → os.EX_IOERR (74), with no frame. Reset never touches TOOLCHAIN, AGENTS, DEPENDENCIES, the bootstrap files or readiness state.
(4) main():
  - append ['reset'] LAST to the argv allowlist tuple;
  - route `if argv == ['reset']: return reset(1)` after the geteuid check, so non-root gets 77;
  - fix the stale comment above the allowlist: openGuestStream (guest-stream.mjs) sends exactly one of these as $SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND.
(5) Header: add a 'Mode reset (CQ-M07f)' paragraph. It reads no stdin, writes {kind: 'reset'} and 0, and lists its codes: 69 a moe-agent or moe-check process is alive (nothing removed), 71 no identity account or no symlink-safe rmtree, 74 a removal or write failure, 77 not root. Add 69 to the taken-codes text. Wrap at 120 columns, and check the new lines only with `git diff -U0 | grep '^+' | awk 'length>121'`.
This moves R13's certified supervisor sha256 (3a19f3bf…). That is expected, and recorded in step 6.

implementationPlan.description:
Teach the host about 'reset'.
(1) scripts/local-runner/guest-ssh.mjs: append 'reset' LAST to SUPERVISOR_MODES. local-runner-bridge.test.mjs GS parity row (around line 2218) parses main()'s allowlist and requires the same order. Update the header bullet about main() accepting exactly SUPERVISOR_MODES only if its wording names the count.
(2) scripts/local-runner/snapshot-transfer.mjs:
  - MODES gains 'reset'.
  - MESSAGES gains TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY: 'The guest still runs a job identity process; its workspace was not reset.'
  - streamOptions accepts an optional frozen `exits` record, defaulting to none, and supervise's close handler uses `transferError(exits && Object.hasOwn(exits, code) ? exits[code] : 'TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED')`. Only reset passes one: `RESET_EXITS = Object.freeze({ 69: 'TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY' })`. So ssh's 255 and every other non-zero exit stay TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED (ruling condition 5).
  - Export `async resetWorkspace({ name, provider = {}, timeoutMs } = {})`. Its onFrame accepts exactly one frame whose keys are exactly ['kind'] and whose kind is 'reset'; anything else is TRANSFER_FRAME_INVALID. It runs `transfer(name, provider, streamOptions({ name, mode: 'reset', provider, timeoutMs, input: [], onFrame, exits: RESET_EXITS }), () => reset)`, so the mounts are checked before and after, and resolves 'reset'.
  - It goes through openGuestStream like every transfer: no fallback, no exec, no host path. The JSDoc says it does not decide WHEN reset runs (CQ-M07j).
Error handling: every outcome is one fixed TRANSFER_* code (INPUT_INVALID, SPAWN_FAILED, TIMEOUT, EXIT_FAILED, RESET_BUSY, FRAME_INVALID, MOUNTS_*).
implementationPlan.note:
guest-ssh.mjs: 'reset' is appended LAST to SUPERVISOR_MODES. The header bullet names no count, so it is unchanged.

snapshot-transfer.mjs:
- 'reset' is added to MODES.
- New message TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY.
- New internal frozen RESET_EXITS = {69: 'TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY'}, not exported.
- streamOptions takes `exits` and refuses with TRANSFER_INPUT_INVALID anything except `undefined`, or RESET_EXITS together with mode 'reset'. Since the object is internal, runSupervisorStream callers can never supply a map (RW3).

- Exported resetWorkspace({name, provider, timeoutMs}):
  - input is [];
  - it accepts exactly one frame whose only key is kind, with value 'reset';
  - it runs transfer(), so mounts are checked before and after, over openGuestStream;

implementationPlan.description:
Rows in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs, in a `// CQ-M07f supervisor reset` section beside the CQ-R09c materialize (M) rows.
- Python rows (RS) call the real supervisor through the existing PY_LOAD / PY_SUPERVISOR harness (`python3 -I -B`, importlib), with injected paths under scratch(t), uids=(os.getuid(),) and an injected alive. As in M1, reset() is never called through main as non-root.
- Plant a full seat state: a materialized workspace (via m.materialize with owner (uid, gid)) plus its manifest, two sessions/home-* dirs with files, and a sessions/other.txt.
- Plant sibling stand-ins for TOOLCHAIN, AGENTS and bootstrap files (bin/moe-supervisor, etc/supervisor.credential), and record their sha256 and modes.

Rows:
- RS1 (DoD 1, 4).
  - reset exits 0, and the out pipe holds exactly one {kind: 'reset'} frame.
  - The workspace, the manifest and both homes are gone, while sessions/ and other.txt remain.
  - Every sibling stand-in is byte- and mode-identical.
  - A following m.materialize into the same paths returns 0.
- RS2 (DoD 2). With alive returning True, the result is 69. Nothing changed (the file list and bytes are equal before and after) and no frame was written. alive got exactly the injected uid set.
- RS3 (DoD 3).
  - Inside the workspace and inside a home, plant symlinks to an OUTSIDE dir and an OUTSIDE file, a symlinked subdir, and a dir chmod 000.
  - After reset (0), the outside dir and file are byte-identical and still exist.
  - A workspace path that is itself a symlink to an outside dir is unlinked, not followed.
- RS4. Refusals:
  - monkeypatch shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks = False: 71, nothing removed;
  - uids None with the pwd lookup patched to KeyError: 71;
  - an alive that raises OSError: 74;
  - a patched os.unlink EIO on the manifest: 74, no frame.
- RS5. main routing.
  - main(['reset'], geteuid=lambda: 0) with m.reset swapped for a recorder returns the recorder's value.
  - geteuid 1000 gives 77.
  - ['reset', 'x'] gives 64.
- RW1 (DoD 5). resetWorkspace over transferProvider fakes:
  - 0 plus {kind: 'reset'} resolves 'reset'; the spawn triple is streamCall('reset'), and the ids show mounts checked before and after;
  - exit 69 → TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY;
  - 64, 65, 71, 74, 77 and 255 → TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED;
  - 0 with no frame, a {kind: 'reset', x: 1} frame, or two frames → TRANSFER_FRAME_INVALID;
  - a transport refusal → TRANSFER_SPAWN_FAILED with no spawn;
  - a late host mount → TRANSFER_MOUNTS_PRESENT.
  Each exercises exactly one spawn: no retry and no fallback.
- RW2. Only the reset mode's map applies. A materialize stream exiting 69 is still TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED.
- RW3. runSupervisorStream({ mode: 'reset', exits: { 255: 'TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY' } }), or any caller-supplied exits that is not RESET_EXITS for the reset mode, is refused with TRANSFER_INPUT_INVALID. That keeps the map internal.

If R14d1's SS9 carrier row is present, add resetWorkspace as its seventh entry point instead of a separate carrier row. Assert exact values, never truthiness. Kill only processes the test spawned. Grep row prefixes before naming.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review, once (skill adversarial-self-review). Then record the pin move.

Review:
- Can reset follow a symlink anywhere: at the workspace root, a session home root, or inside either? Is the fd-based rmtree enforced?
- Can a job identity race the probe? Reset runs between jobs under the host's job lease, and a guest with no live identity process has nothing to start one. Say so in a comment.
- Is anything removed when busy? Is anything outside the three targets touched?
- Is 69 unique? Is 255 never mapped? Could the exits map be supplied by a caller?
- Is every existing guarantee kept, including materialize's EX_CANTCREAT and the readiness probes (task rail)?
- Would a mutant that drops the busy check, uses a following removal, unlinks sessions/ itself or maps every exit to RESET_BUSY survive? Kill each with a row.
- Does the diff list only the four planned files?

Then record the pin move:
- Post a comment on task-f4811a729f9e436ba129a65c12d348c1 (R13) and on task-1a8f1d0e199046a289e94a5453d758b8 (CQ-M07). It names the new guest-supervisor.py sha256 from step 4, the commit-to-be, and that it supersedes 3a19f3bf… for the operator's re-certify.

implementationPlan.note:
Ran the adversarial self-review on the task's 5 paths. That is the 4 planned files plus certificationEvidence.ts, which comment-c3fe4480 authorized.

- Symlinks: remove_entry uses lstat, so a link is unlinked as itself. Directories go only through shutil.rmtree, and reset refuses with 71 unless rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks. If a path is swapped for a link between the lstat and the rmtree, the fd-based rmtree raises OSError, which gives 74, and nothing is followed. RS3 covers links inside the workspace and a home, a home that is itself a link, and a workspace or manifest that is a link.
- Races: reset runs between jobs under the host's job lease (R06). With no moe-agent or moe-check process alive, nothing in the guest can start one, so the /proc probe cannot be raced. This is written in the code comment above reset(). /var/lib/moe and SESSIONS (0711) are root's, so a job cannot swap them.
- When busy: alive() runs before any removal, so code 69 removes nothing and writes no frame (RS2). Only WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MANIFEST and SESSIONS/home-* are removed; RS1 shows every other byte and mode survives.
- Exit codes: 69 is unique; HEAD had no EX_UNAVAILABLE. RESET_EXITS is frozen, module-private and maps only 69, so 255 and signal or null codes stay TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED (RW1, RW2). A caller-supplied exits map is refused before any provider call (RW3).
- Kept guarantees: the main allowlist is only appended to, and materialize EX_CANTCREAT and the readiness probes are untouched. GS1 parity is green.
- Mutants: every mutant the plan named is killed (see step-3). Dropping only `mode === 'reset'` from the guard is equivalent.
- Theoretical, no fix: a zombie job process counts as alive, which is the safe direction (busy, retry). A malformed /proc Uid line would raise ValueError, giving exit 1 and EXIT_FAILED, which fails closed.

Pin move posted: R13 comment-a7f0756a and CQ-M07 comment-fa0f6000 name 616463b7d33cf5d0efa79d5540d0911a5c56a6899b63b244ce60116e1aec0c0e, which supersedes 3a19f3bf….

comments.author: architect-b520bc90
comments.content:
PLAN CORRECTION, rev 1 (architect-b520bc90): leave the "dir chmod 000" element out of RS3.

**Why.** The RS rows run as a non-root user. A non-root owner cannot list a mode-000 directory, so shutil.rmtree would raise EACCES there and reset would correctly return 74. Root in the guest bypasses directory modes, so the case only means something under root.

**What RS3 keeps.** The links-to-outside cases:
- a symlink inside the workspace and inside a home, to an outside dir and to an outside file;
- a symlinked subdir;
- a workspace root that is itself a symlink.

**Also, on step 2's `exits`.** The map is internal. runSupervisorStream must refuse an `exits` key from its caller with TRANSFER_INPUT_INVALID (RW3), and only resetWorkspace passes RESET_EXITS to streamOptions.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
The guest supervisor gains a root-only `reset` mode. It reads no stdin.
- It refuses with 69 (nothing removed) while any process of moe-agent or moe-check exists, by /proc uid scan.
- It refuses with 71 when an identity account is missing or the interpreter's rmtree cannot avoid symlink attacks.
- Otherwise it removes WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MANIFEST and every sessions/home-* entry without following links, writes {kind: 'reset'} and exits 0. Removal or write failure is 74, not root is 77.
The host's resetWorkspace runs it through openGuestStream between two mount checks. Outcomes: 0 plus the frame is 'reset', 69 is TRANSFER_RESET_BUSY, and any other exit (ssh's 255 included) is TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED, with no fallback.
invariants: Reset never touches TOOLCHAIN, AGENTS, DEPENDENCIES, the bootstrap files, readiness state or the sessions directory itself.
Materialize, export, verify, agents, toolchain, dependencies, bridge and check behavior and codes are unchanged. Readiness and certified-provider.json are untouched (task rail).
SUPERVISOR_MODES equals main()'s allowlist in order, with 'reset' last.
Only the reset stream maps an exit code to anything but TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED, through the internal RESET_EXITS map. A caller cannot supply a map.
compatibility: Existing transfer entry points and runSupervisorStream keep their signatures. An omitted exits keeps today's mapping.
R13's certified supervisor sha256 (3a19f3bf…) moves on purpose. The new sha is posted on R13 and CQ-M07 for the single operator re-certify.
sourceAssumptions: guest-supervisor.py: main(argv, geteuid, **seams) has a literal allowlist tuple and the geteuid check. materialize returns EX_CANTCREAT for an existing workspace or manifest. session_home makes sessions/home-* via mkdtemp, chowned to the job uid. WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MANIFEST, SESSIONS, AGENT_IDENTITY and CHECK_IDENTITY are module constants.
local-runner-bridge.test.mjs (around line 2218) asserts SUPERVISOR_MODES equals the main() allowlist parsed from the .py.

snapshot-transfer.mjs: transfer() wraps supervise between two assertNoMounts calls, and verifyWorkspace is the shape to mirror (input [], one exact frame). After R14d1, supervise opens through openGuestStream.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected alternatives:
- A hand-written fd walk instead of shutil.rmtree. Python 3.12's rmtree is fd-based with avoids_symlink_attacks on Linux, and reset refuses (71) where it is not.
- A busy check through pgrep. That needs procps and a PATH lookup inside the trusted supervisor, while a /proc uid scan is stdlib only.
- Mapping every non-zero exit to EXIT_FAILED. CQ-M07j needs to tell 'a job identity survived the sweep' apart from failure.
